gaps.lead: She prefers reading books to watching television.
gaps.explanation: prefer X to Y = would rather do X than do Y.

gaps.lead: The film we saw last week was better than this one.
gaps.sentence: This film is not ___ the one we saw last week.
gaps.explanation: 'Not as good as' expresses an inferior comparison.

gaps.answer: invited him to join them for
gaps.lead: 'Would you like to join us for dinner?' they asked him.
gaps.explanation: invite somebody TO do something; pronouns shift in reporting.

gaps.lead: I'd prefer it if you arrived before eight.
gaps.explanation: would rather + subject + past simple for other people's actions.

gaps.lead: You can borrow the car, but you must drive it carefully.
gaps.sentence: You can borrow the car ___ it carefully.

gaps.lead: He no longer thinks he can find a job before the end of the year.
gaps.sentence: He has given ___ a job before the end of the year.
gaps.explanation: 'No longer thinks he can find' becomes 'has given up hope of finding'.

gaps.lead: It would be sensible to leave before the traffic builds up.
gaps.sentence: We ___ before the traffic builds up.
gaps.explanation: 'It would be sensible to do' = 'we had better do' — had better + bare infinitive.

gaps.lead: She'll be on a flight, so she can't join the call.
gaps.sentence: She'll be on a flight, so ___ join the call.
gaps.explanation: won't be able to = future inability.
